summary: Devendra Nath Ojha is an Indologist who completed a certificate in Jyotisha at National Sanskrit University in 2020. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Delhi (2011–2013) and Assistant Professor and HoD of Sanskrit at Amity University (2017).
Deviprasad Mishra is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the French Institute of Pondicherry in 1999. That same year, he served there as a researcher and Deputy Head of Indology.
Dewei Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dhananjay Vashistha works in Indology and philosophy after earning a B.E. (Hons) from BITS Pilani (2011–2015). Formerly a network engineer at Cisco Systems and faculty at Trans IAS Academy, he became a Research Associate at Bhaktivedanta Research Center in 2023.

Dharm P. S. Bhawuk works in Indology and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1995 and was appointed affiliate faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa that same year.

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (1926) and held posts at the University of Calcutta, Harvard University, Gujarat University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1923). He held academic posts at Patna College in 1928 and at the University of Minnesota from 1951 to 1952.
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and the traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held teaching posts at the Open University, University of Leeds, and University of Bristol, and joined the University of Chester in 2019.
Di Jiang is a scholar in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo specializes in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA and by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge for a PhD, Luo graduated from the University of Southern California (attested 2016).

Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1976 until becoming emerita around 2024.

Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, EPHE, and Sorbonne, and held posts at TU Berlin, Leipzig, Zurich, Museum am Rothenbaum, MPIWG, Humboldt, and Hamburg.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Denis specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a BA from Naropa University (1989–1995) and a PhD from Laval University (2005–2013), and served as an Associate Professor at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 2017.

Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford. She held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College (attested 2010), and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who conducted graduate studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).
